prompt.context: Your client is Nickel Inc., a company in the nickel enrichment industry in Brazil. Its business consists of: purchasing brute nickel and nickel additives from producers; transporting them to Nickel Inc.'s plant in Southern Brazil; enriching the brute nickel at the plant; and delivering the enriched nickel to factories in Southeastern Brazil. Nickel Inc. is currently the #3 nickel enrichment company in Brazil, producing a total of 10 tons of enriched nickel per month. Due to increasing demand, Nickel Inc. wants to increase its production to 20 tons per month.
prompt.question: How should Nickel Inc. increase its production from 10 to 20 tons of enriched nickel per month?

clarifying_info.q: Is this purely a cost analysis or do we also consider revenue?
clarifying_info.a: This is a cost case. No revenue analysis is needed.

clarifying_info.q: Are there constraints on capital or financing?
clarifying_info.a: The company has the ability to invest; we will explore the financial implications as we go.

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeline for the production increase?
clarifying_info.a: No specific timeline has been given beyond wanting to increase production.

framework: Brainstorm ways to increase production (utilize existing plant vs. utilize another plant)
Narrow down to two options: expand existing plant in Southern Brazil vs. build a new plant in Southeastern Brazil
Identify relevant financial factors: variable costs per input, fixed costs, and initial investment for each option
Calculate variable cost per ton of enriched nickel for each option using input proportions
Calculate total monthly cost to produce the additional 10 tons (variable + fixed) for each option
Compare monthly savings of the cheaper option against the incremental initial investment to derive payback period
Consider qualitative factors and risks before making a recommendation

questions.prompt: Question 1: What are some ways in which Nickel Inc. can increase its production?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm both organic and inorganic options. Key buckets: (1) Utilize existing plant — increase efficiency or expand the plant. (2) Utilize another plant — build a new plant, acquire a competitor, or form a joint venture/subcontract.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Nickel Inc. has determined that the only two alternatives are expanding its existing plant or building a new plant in Southeastern Brazil. What factors would you consider in deciding between these two options?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should cover: (1) Costs — variable and fixed costs, plus initial investment required for each option. (2) Location advantage — the new plant would be closer to the factories in Southeastern Brazil, potentially reducing transportation/delivery costs. (3) Input cost differences — costs of nickel and additives may differ by location due to different suppliers and transport distances. (4) Economies of scale — one plant producing 20 tons may be more efficient than two plants producing 10 tons each. (5) Operational complexity — running two plants may incur additional management and overhead costs.

questions.prompt: Question 3: Given the financial data, calculate the cost of producing the additional 10 tons per month under each option, and determine how long it takes for the cheaper option to pay back its extra investment.
questions.guidance: Candidate must compute variable cost per ton using the input proportions, then add fixed costs for 10 incremental tons, compare total monthly costs, and calculate the payback period for the higher-investment option.

math.setup:
To produce 1 ton of enriched nickel: 0.67 ton brute nickel + 0.10 ton sulfur + 0.05 ton other additives.

Expand existing plant — input prices: brute nickel $270,000/ton, sulfur $150,000/ton, other additives $100,000/ton. Fixed costs $200,000/month. Initial investment $2,000,000.

Build new plant — input prices: brute nickel $150,000/ton, sulfur $200,000/ton, other additives $200,000/ton. Fixed costs $700,000/month. Initial investment $10,000,000.
steps: Monthly cost for 10 extra tons — Expand: (200,000 × 10) + 200,000 = $2,200,000/month
Monthly cost for 10 extra tons — Build New: (130,000 × 10) + 700,000 = $2,000,000/month
Monthly savings from building new vs. expanding: $2,200,000 − $2,000,000 = $200,000/month
math.answer: Building a new plant saves $200,000 per month relative to expanding the existing plant, but requires $8,000,000 more in upfront investment. The extra investment pays back in 40 months.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways Nickel Inc. can increase its production from 10 to 20 tons per month?

categories.name: Utilize existing plant
ideas: Increase operational efficiency (reduce downtime, optimize shift schedules)
Expand the existing plant (add capacity at current site)

categories.name: Utilize another plant
ideas: Build a new plant in Southeastern Brazil (closer to customers)
Acquire a competitor with spare capacity
Form a joint venture or subcontract to a third-party enrichment facility

recommendation: If Nickel Inc. can tolerate a 40-month payback horizon and has access to $10M in capital, it should build a new plant in Southeastern Brazil, as it generates $200,000/month in cost savings once operational and positions the company closer to its factory customers.
If capital is constrained or the payback period is too long, expanding the existing plant is the preferred option with a lower upfront investment of $2,000,000.
risks: Running two separate plants (existing + expanded) adds operational complexity and management overhead.
A new plant requires additional construction time before production can begin, delaying the production increase.
Not having a plant proximate to Southeastern Brazil factories may hurt customer relationships if delivery times or logistics costs remain high under the expansion option.
Commodity price assumptions for inputs (nickel, sulfur, additives) may shift, altering the cost comparison.
next_steps: Assess Nickel Inc.'s available capital and financing options to determine affordability of the $10M investment.
Estimate the construction timeline for a new plant vs. the expansion timeline to understand the production ramp-up delay.
Model sensitivity of the 40-month payback to input price fluctuations and demand scenarios.
Evaluate the strategic value of proximity to Southeastern Brazil factories and potential revenue/retention implications.
